title: Tamsin and the Kitchen
premise: Isandro Ashgrove, a wedding planner who swore off believing in love after her own family imploded, hires struggling baker Tamsin Vey to pose as her girlfriend for her sister's reunion-weekend wedding. What begins as a transactional lie deepens as Tamsin's bakery faces eviction by a developer who turns out to be Isandro's own uncle, forcing Isandro to choose between the family that funds her career and the woman who makes her want to stop hiding. At the climax, Isandro must publicly say the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade—'My family was wrong, and so was I'—to save Tamsin's lease, sacrificing her inheritance and her reputation. The book ends a year later with the two of them planning a wedding that Isandro, for the first time, actually believes in: their own, small and unglamorous, above the bakery.
about_author: Noor Zhou is a former pastry chef turned writer who lives above a bakery she refuses to name, for privacy's sake. She writes love stories about people who negotiate their way into courage one small, safe step at a time.

chapters.title: The Contract of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet her mid-wedding, flawlessly executing a stranger's perfect day while privately believing none of it. A phone call summons her to her sister's reunion wedding, where she must bring a plus-one or admit she's been alone for years. Beat: competent armor, quiet dread.

chapters.title: Flour and Emergency
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin's bakery is three missed rent payments from eviction; a caterer just canceled on the Ashgrove reunion. Isandro walks in with an absurd offer: fake girlfriend, real pay, one weekend. Tamsin laughs her out of the shop. Beat: desperation disguised as pride.

chapters.title: The Price of a Weekend
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The developer's final notice arrives—sixty days. Tamsin finds Isandro's card and calls, negotiating terms like a hostile merger: no real names in the story, no kissing, no questions about the past. Beat: a deal struck out of survival, both women lying to themselves.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Unrehearsed Hearts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The reunion begins at the family estate; Isandro coaches Tamsin on her invented biography over the car ride. Tamsin improvises so well she embarrasses Isandro's critical mother. Beat: the fake starts working too well, and Isandro notices she's watching Tamsin instead of performing.

chapters.title: Dessert Was a Mistake
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin supplies the reunion's dessert course and watches Isandro's family dismiss her work. Isandro publicly defends the cake—small, but seismic. Later, alone in the kitchen, the almost-kiss they agreed against nearly happens. Beat: the lie curdles into something real by dessert, exactly as feared.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Flashback woven through a sleepless night: the scandal that broke her family, the sentence her father made her rehearse—'My family was wrong, and so was I'—which she refused to say and paid for with fifteen years of exile-in-plain-sight. Beat: the reader learns the cost of her silence.

chapters.title: The Uncle Who Buys Streets
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin learns the developer threatening her bakery is Marcus Ashgrove—Isandro's uncle and the family's money. She confronts Isandro, who genuinely didn't know but now can't un-know it. Beat: trust cracks; the fake relationship acquires real stakes and real conflict.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro tries to fix it quietly through family channels and is humiliated by Marcus, who offers to save the bakery if Isandro finally comes back into the fold—on his terms, with her silence intact. She doesn't tell Tamsin about the offer. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: A Real Date, Falsely Advertised
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Between reunion events, the two steal an actual afternoon—farmers' market, bad coffee, honest laughter. Tamsin realizes she's stopped keeping score of what's fake. Beat: falling, and hating how easily it's happening.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Her sister Priya corners her: she knows the relationship is staged—she found the contract. Instead of exposing them, Priya asks why Isandro needs a lie to come home. Beat: the reunion's real antagonist revealed as Isandro's own avoidance.

chapters.title: Kiss, Uncontracted
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. After a family toast turns cruel, Isandro and Tamsin escape to the estate gardens and kiss—off-script, off-contract, undeniable. They agree to extend the arrangement indefinitely, both pretending it's still pretend. Beat: peak sweetness before the fall.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro digs into Marcus's development filings and finds the bakery's block is a lynchpin he's been hiding from the family partnership. She also finds evidence her father's old scandal was Marcus's doing—and that her silence protected the wrong man. Beat: justice and love begin to point the same direction.

chapters.title: The Offer on the Table
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Marcus approaches Tamsin directly: a generous buyout, relocation money, and a hint that Isandro already knew about his offer. Tamsin, stung, confronts Isandro, who admits the omission. Beat: the fake relationship's first real betrayal-shaped wound.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro weighs Marcus's terms—her career, her inheritance, her family's acceptance—in exchange for letting the bakery die quietly. She drafts an acceptance letter. Beat: the lowest point; the old reflex to stay invisible wins for a moment.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin bakes alone at 3 a.m., deciding whether to take the buyout and survive, or fight and maybe lose everything. She finds Isandro's unsigned acceptance letter left in the bakery office. Beat: heartbreak, and the clarity that follows it.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro stands before her father's old study mirror and says the sentence aloud for the first time in fifteen years. It doesn't kill her. She burns Marcus's offer and calls Priya: she's going to speak at the reunion's final toast. Beat: the decision that changes everything.

chapters.title: Toast at the Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, scene-level. Before two hundred guests, Isandro says it publicly: 'My family was wrong, and so was I'—naming Marcus's betrayal, renouncing her inheritance, and announcing the bakery fight. Marcus threatens ruin; Priya stands up beside her. Beat: climax; the sentence finally spoken, the decade's price paid in one breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fallout: clients flee Isandro's company, the family splits, and Tamsin learns what Isandro sacrificed. Tamsin shows up not to thank her but to fight beside her—organizing the neighborhood, the press, the lease battle. Beat: love as partnership, not rescue.

chapters.title: The Lease Hearing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the zoning hearing, Isandro deploys everything she learned from Marcus's own filings; Priya's testimony seals it. The development plan collapses; the bakery's lease is renewed on fair terms. Beat: justice outside the law, won with paper and nerve.

chapters.title: Rebuilding, Honestly
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later: Isandro broke and rebuilding her business from a desk in the bakery's back room. They take down the old fake-dating contract and, instead of tearing it up, amend it—one handwritten clause at a time. Beat: tender, funny, earned intimacy.

chapters.title: The Question in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the bakery's one-year anniversary of the hearing, Tamsin proposes—not grandly, but with a ring baked into a test loaf and a speech about small safe steps. Isandro, who doesn't believe in weddings anymore, says yes before Tamsin finishes. Beat: love against duty, duty finally released.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Believing
chapters.summary: Both POVs, braided. The epilogue-wedding: forty guests, above the bakery, no seating chart, Isandro crying through her own vows and Tamsin's imperfect cake. Isandro realizes she planned a thousand weddings to learn what this one needed: the truth. Beat: resolution; the price paid, the life kept.
